Communicable Diseases in Children

Childhood communicable diseases — chickenpox, measles, mumps, pertussis and others, with nursing care and immunisation.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe the common exanthemata and their incubation
  • Give nursing care for infectious children
  • Explain isolation and droplet precautions
  • Link immunisation to prevention

In simple words

Communicable diseases spread from person to person. In children, clusters of fever with rash (exanthemata) and respiratory infections are common — and mostly preventable by vaccination.

Common childhood communicable diseases

Disease Incubation Rash or feature
Measles 10-14 days Maculopapular rash from hairline; three Cs
Chickenpox (varicella) 14-16 days Crops of vesicles; very itchy
Mumps 16-18 days Painful parotid swelling
Rubella 14-21 days Pink maculopapular rash; danger in pregnancy
Diphtheria 2-5 days Grey throat membrane; bull neck
Pertussis (whooping cough) 7-14 days Paroxysmal cough with whoop and vomiting
Polio 3-35 days Asymmetric flaccid paralysis
Roseola infantum 5-15 days High fever then sudden pink rash

Nursing care of infectious children

  • Isolation according to route (airborne, droplet, contact)
  • Comfort — light clothing, soft diet, cool room, prune nails to prevent scratching
  • Itch control in chickenpox — cold compresses, trim nails, gloves at night
  • Monitor temperature, feeding, swallowing and breathing
  • Prevent secondary infection — mouth care, skin care, hand hygiene
  • Support the family — explain home isolation, vaccination of siblings
  • Report notifiable diseases to authorities

🔴 Never give aspirin in chickenpox or influenza

Aspirin is avoided in children with viral illness because of Reye syndrome (liver and brain swelling). Use paracetamol for fever.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Measles rash starts at the hairline and spreads downwards.
  2. Chickenpox has crops of vesicles that progress from macule to scab.
  3. Chickenpox is infectious 2 days before the rash.
  4. Pertussis causes paroxysmal cough with whoop and post-tussive vomiting.
  5. Rubella in early pregnancy can harm the fetus.
  6. Aspirin is avoided in viral illness because of Reye syndrome.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Measles incubation is 10-14 days.
  2. Varicella isolation continues until all lesions crust.
  3. Mumps causes bilateral parotid swelling with pain on chewing.
  4. Pertussis isolation lasts until 5 days of antibiotics.
  5. Vaccines under UIP prevent measles, mumps, pertussis and polio.

📌 Memory trick

Exanthemata mnemonic for rash order: chickenpox vesicles, measles maculopapular from the head.

60-second revision

  • Measles, chickenpox, mumps, rubella, roseola: characteristic rashes.
  • Pertussis: paroxysmal cough, whoop, vomiting.
  • Diphtheria: grey membrane; polio: flaccid paralysis.
  • Care: isolate, comfort, itch control, fever control, mouth care.
  • No aspirin; vaccinate; report notifiable diseases.

Test yourself

A child has crops of very itchy vesicles spreading from the trunk. This is:

Answer: B. Chickenpox appears as successive crops of itchy vesicles, macules, papules and scabs together.

The measles rash begins:

Answer: B. The measles rash begins behind the ears and on the hairline and spreads downwards.

Paroxysmal cough with a whoop suggests:

Answer: B. Pertussis (whooping cough) gives paroxysms of cough with a whoop and vomiting.

Why is aspirin avoided in viral illness in children?

Answer: B. Aspirin in viral illness can cause Reye syndrome with liver damage and encephalopathy.

Chickenpox is infectious from:

Answer: B. Chickenpox spreads from about 2 days before the rash until all lesions have crusted.
